audit.whatIsWrong: The chart handed Shen levels 3, 4-5 and first item while the whys on those same rows say your full mark kit is online, that you keep the poke edge, and that first item is 'close to even'.
audit.why: 50.74% over 272 games with Kennen's range advantage early: he owns 2-3 and level 6, the middle rows are even, and only the late game is genuinely Shen's.
audit.corrected: Rows re-sided in matched pairs to Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Kennen / Skill / Shen. Row 6 deliberately kept as Shen against the packet's 'Skill' because whys[6] and late both state he out-scales outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: First item was written as a Kennen spike to force fights on.
audit.why: Shen is buying HP and MR into that window and Spirit's Refuge eats the auto component of your combo, so the item spike does not hand you the lane — the content layer already said so.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten to an even window; the level-6 stun-lock stays the one clear spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shen's ultimate is called 'Stand Strong' in six places, Spirit's Refuge is described as eating your marks generally, and wants.foe[0] claims his taunt 'turns off your R mid-cast'.
audit.why: The ultimate is Stand United. Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks — basic attacks only — so Thundering Shuriken, Electrical Surge's active and Slicing Maelstrom all still land through it; only the auto-attack half of your mark stacking stalls. And Kennen's R carries no channel flag: a taunt drags you toward Shen, it does not switch the storm off.
audit.corrected: Name fixed everywhere, Spirit's Refuge stated as basic-attacks-only, and the taunt restated as being dragged into his team.
sources: enemyKit W text 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked'

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page says Stand United is interruptible.
audit.why: Shen's R carries the channel flag — any CC cancels it. Kennen's passive stuns on the third Mark of the Storm, so a completed mark chain on Shen cancels a global that was about to save a diving teammate. That is the single highest-value thing Kennen does to Shen and it was absent.
sources: enemyKit R flags: channel 'interruptible — any CC cancels it'

audit.whatIsWrong: Shadow Dash was tracked as a generic 'engage CC' with no number.
audit.why: It is 18/16/14/12/10 at 600 range and costs 150 mana — the longest punish window in his kit, and Twilight Assault's 140 mana at rank 1 means he cannot spam either.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and ranges written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and whys[2].
sources: enemyKit E and Q cooldowns, ranges and costs

edits.before: Shen has no Shadow Dash until level 2 and no real damage, so levels 1-3 are your cleanest window — Thundering Shuriken (Q) his last-hits and let Electrical Surge autos chip while he has no taunt to punish you. The moment he points his E, every trade is about its cooldown: poke freely when it's down, give nothing when it's up because a taunt cancels your whole pattern. Watch for Spirit's Refuge (W) — that bubble blocks your auto marks, so it stalls your third-stack stun if you walk in dumb.
edits.after: Shadow Dash is an 18-second cooldown at rank 1 and Twilight Assault costs 140 mana, so levels 1-3 are your cleanest window — Thundering Shuriken (Q) his last-hits and let Electrical Surge autos chip him while his mana is thin. Once E is up, every trade is about its cooldown: poke freely when it's down, give nothing when it's up because a taunt drags you into everything. Spirit's Refuge (W) blocks basic attacks only, so inside it keep stacking marks with Q rather than walking in.

edits.before: Level 6 is your spike and the one window you clearly own: Q-W to stack marks, E in (or Flash), and Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks him before he can Shadow Dash off it. But Shen trades evenly the rest of mid-game — he's tanky, he sustains, and his taunt flips any extended fight, so don't autopilot all-ins on his Shadow Dash being up. The real danger here isn't the 1v1; it's his Stand Strong (R) shipping him across the map, so respect that he can vanish from lane and your dive timing onto a Shen who R'd out is wasted.
edits.after: Level 6 is your spike and the one window you clearly own: Q-W to stack marks, E in (or Flash), and Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks him before he can Shadow Dash off it. Shen trades evenly the rest of mid-game — he's tanky, he sustains, and his taunt flips any extended fight, so don't autopilot all-ins while that 18s E is up. The real danger isn't the 1v1; it's Stand United (R) shipping him across the map on a 200s cooldown, so a dive onto a Shen who already R'd out is wasted.

edits.before: This goes even because Shen scales into exactly what you don't — a global, peel-tank teamfighter who is tankier than your magic burst can kill once he has items and MR. Your squishy short-cooldown caster body wants you to find the pick and stun-lock before he reaches the fight, so play engager off your R and force fights while his Stand Strong is on cooldown. If you can't kill him, don't feed him — chunk his carries through his taunt window and let your team clean up, because a fed late Shen with R up decides skirmishes you'll never be present for.
edits.after: This goes even because Shen scales into exactly what you don't — a global, peel-tank teamfighter who is tankier than your magic burst can kill once he has items and MR. Your squishy short-cooldown caster body wants the pick before he reaches the fight, so play engager off your R and force fights while Stand United's 200s cooldown is running. Better still, if he starts the channel across the map, land your third mark and cancel it. If you can't kill him, chunk his carries through the taunt window instead.

notes: Shen's ultimate was named 'Stand Strong' in six fields; the real name is Stand United and it is a 200/180/160 channel, so a Mark of the Storm stun cancels it — the highest-value interaction in the matchup and it was missing entirely. Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks only, which the page overstated as eating your marks; Q, W-active and R all land through it. packet.suspectNames flags 'Time Spirit's Refuge' in wants.foe[1] as a wrong ability name — it is a false positive, the sentence reads 'Time Spirit's Refuge (W) to block...' with 'Time' as the verb. Left untouched. Row 6 of the chart kept as Shen rather than the packet's 'Skill' because both whys[6] and the late paragraph state he out-scales outright.
